kilauea_notices.title: HAWAIIAN VOLCANO OBSERVATORY DAILY UPDATE
kilauea_notices.message: HVO Kilauea YELLOW/ADVISORY - The Halema'uma'u eruption at the summit of Kīlauea is paused following lava fountaining episode 57 on the morning of November 23. Preliminary forecast models suggest the next episode may occur sometime between December 3 and 16.
kilauea_notices.detail: Overview: Last night, glow was observed at both the north and southwest eruptive vents in Halema'uma'u, where strong degassing has persisted since the end of Kīlauea summit lava fountaining episode 57 on November 23. All summit tiltmeters show inflation resuming when episode 57 ended, indicating that another episode is likely in the coming weeks. Preliminary forecast models suggest that the next episode may occur sometime between December 3 and 16; this window will be refined as more tilt data are incorporated into the models. Details and a chronology of lava fountaining episode 57 are included in a status report here: https://volcanoes.usgs.gov/hans-public/notice/DOI-USGS-HVO-2026-11-23T17:33:15+00:00 Summit Observations: Summit webcams recorded moderate, consistent glow at the southwest vent and weaker, intermittent glow at the north vent overnight. Lava flows on the floor of Halemaʻumaʻu crater still exhibit scattered points of incandescence as they cool and solidify in the aftermath of lava fountaining episode 57, though they may not last much longer. Slumping of tephra deposits on the southeast side of the eruptive vent complex slowed yesterday and appears to have stopped moving overnight. Since the end of lava fountaining episode 57 on November 23, the Uēkahuna tiltmeter (UWD) has recorded approximately 7.0 microradians of inflationary tilt, after recording approximately 18 microradians of deflationary tilt during the episode. Other summit tiltmeters also showed a rapid change from deflationary tilt to inflationary tilt when lava fountaining concluded. However, the rate of inflation is gradually slowing, as often observed between episodes. In the aftermath of lava fountaining episode 57, seismicity has followed a normal pattern by returning to low-level tremor with tremor bursts becoming more erratic this morning. Only one earthquake was located within the summit region over the past day. The Halemaʻumaʻu eruptive vents continue emitting a robust plume of volcanic gases. Winds are currently out of the west, but they are expected to become more northeasterly today, eventually blowing the gas plume to the southwest. The Hawaiian Volcano Observatory's array of gas instruments southwest of the eruptive vents measured a sulfur dioxide (SO2) emission rate of approximately 2,100 tonnes per day on Tuesday afternoon, November 24. Rift Zone Observations: Rates of seismicity and ground deformation remain low in the East Rift Zone and Southwest Rift Zone. SO2 emissions from the East Rift Zone remain below instrumental detection limits. Analysis: Since the end of lava fountaining episode 57 on November 23, summit tiltmeters have recorded a typical post-fountaining recovery with nearly continuous inflationary tilt, albeit at a slowing rate. The abrupt switch from summit deflation to inflation at the end of the episode, continued glow from the eruptive vents, and the resumption of low-frequency seismic tremor bursts indicate that another lava fountaining episode is likely in the coming weeks. Preliminary forecast models suggest that the next episode may occur sometime between December 3 and 16; this window will be refined as more tilt data are incorporated into the models. Kīlauea has been erupting episodically since December 23, 2024, from two primary vents (north and south) within Halemaʻumaʻu at the summit. Lava fountaining episodes generally last less than 12 hours and are separated by pauses of two or more weeks. HVO continues to closely monitor Kīlauea and remains in contact with Hawaiʻi Volcanoes National Park and the Hawaiʻi County Civil Defense Agency regarding eruptive hazards. Summary of episode 57 (Episode 57 Status Report): Lava fountaining occurred between 12:15 a.m. and 6:00 a.m. on November 23, 2026. Maximum fountain heights were about 660 feet (200 meters). mauna_loa_notices.title: HAWAIIAN VOLCANO OBSERVATORY MONTHLY UPDATE
mauna_loa_notices.message: HVO Mauna Loa GREEN/NORMAL - Mauna Loa earthquake counts were within typical levels in October, and minor inflation continues.
mauna_loa_notices.detail: Mauna Loa had a slight increase in seismic activity compared to the previous month; a total of 66 earthquakes were detected in Mauna Loa's summit region during the October reporting period, after 53 in September. These variations are within the typical range for the past two years. Most earthquakes occurred deep beneath the upper Southwest Rift Zone or broadly scattered around the upper flanks. Data from Global Positioning System (GPS) instruments on Mauna Loa showed slight inflation across the summit region in the past month. Oscillations between contraction and inflation patterns during non-eruptive periods are normal, but inflation has been the dominant trend since the 2022 eruption, consistent with magma refilling the summit reservoir system. Gas and temperature data from a station on Mauna Loa's Southwest Rift Zone indicate these values are at background levels, with little change relative to previous months. HVO continues to closely monitor Mauna Loa and will issue another update in one month, or earlier, should conditions change significantly.
